question: A 2-year-old child presents to the clinic with complaints of difficulty walking and easy fatigability. After a detailed history, examination, and relevant investigations it is found that the child has low blood glucose, hypotonia, muscle weakness, and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Which of the following disease is characterized by these clinical manifestations?

A mother brings her 10-year-old child to the clinic saying that her child is taller than other children his age and that his limbs are abnormally long. In history, the mother tells that she conceived him at the age of 37 years. Examination findings reveal that the child has tall stature and his height is greater than the 90th percentile. The scrotal sac is empty indicating an undescended testis. The IQ of the child is 110. What is the most likely diagnosis?
What is the ratio of chest compressions to breaths in one cycle during cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) in neonates with a single rescuer present on site?
A child is born to an HBsAg-positive mother. On examination, the child looks normal and there is no yellowish discoloration of the skin. How will you manage the further immunization of this child?

answers.option: Give him Hepatitis B Immune Globulin (HBIG) 1 mL intramuscular, hepatitis B vaccine at 0, 1, and 6 months
Give him the usual hepatitis B vaccine at 0, 1, and 6 months
No Hepatitis B Immune Globulin (HBIG) or hepatitis B vaccine needed
Give him Hepatitis B Immune Globulin (HBIG) 0.5 mL intramuscular, hepatitis B vaccine at 0, 1, and 6 months
Only give him Hepatitis B Immune Globulin (HBIG) 2 ml intramuscular

question: A 4-year-old child comes to the emergency room with complaints of generalized seizures. On further inquiry, the mother reveals that the child has had an undocumented high-grade fever for two days. Examination reveals a fever of 103°F  (39.4°C), signs of meningeal irritation, and upgoing plantar reflexes. What is the most likely diagnosis?

The mother of a 5-month-old child comes to the outpatient department requesting vitamin supplements for her child. She is concerned that her child is not getting enough vitamins since he is exclusively breastfed. What will you prescribe to the child?

An 8-year-old boy presents to the emergency department with a complaint of high-grade fever for 5 days. The mother complains that his urine output has been significantly less and he had several episodes of bloody diarrhea. On examination, the child is ill-looking, pale, and febrile with edema on both the extremities and crepitations in both lung bases. Laboratory investigations show low hemoglobin and platelet count.  What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 10-year-old boy presents to the outpatient department for his follow-up due to a certain congenital heart defect. The child tells you that he has learned that whenever he squats in response to a cyanotic episode, the episode gets better. Which of the following is a finding in this disease?

answers.option: Pansystolic murmur at the tip of sternum
Flow murmur at left second intercostal space

question: A 7-year-old boy presents to the emergency department due to difficulty breathing after he fell off a bicycle. On examination, there is decreased chest movement, decreased breath sound, and hyper-resonance on the right side of the chest. The mediastinal shift is towards the left. A chest x-ray is requested . What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 5-year-old boy is brought by his mother that he has been remaining inattentive in class and his academic performance is faltering. During the examination, the child starts staring blankly at the examiner for about 30 seconds. An electroencephalogram (EEG) is performed and it shows 3 Hz and spike-wave discharge. Which of the following drugs is the first-line treatment used for this condition?

A 9-year-old presents to the clinic with a history of fever, and a vesicular rash on the trunk and extremities for 5 days. His father reveals that several other members of the family have the same complaint. The pediatrician suspects chickenpox. Which of the following is a complication of chickenpox?

The mother of a 4-year-old child is concerned because she has found him eating dirt off the floor on several occasions. The doctor informs the mother that this condition is called pica, and it is often due to a nutritional deficiency. Which of the following nutritional deficiency causes pica?

A mother has brought her 8-year-old girl because of bilateral lower limb weakness for 3 days. She has a history of dysentery 3 weeks back. The weakness is equal on both limbs and is moving proximally. On examination, the child has absent deep tendon reflexes in the lower limb. Which of the following statements is correct regarding the following disease?

answers.option: Increase in total nucleated cell count and normal total protein concentration on cerebrospinal fuild analysis
No association with a systemic infection
CT Scan is the gold standard investigation
Diagnosis is by nerve conduction studies

question: A 5-year-old girl comes to the emergency department with complaints of vomiting, difficulty breathing, and blood-tinged diarrhea following ingestion of kerosene. What is the best initial management in this case?

answers.option: Gastric lavage with a cuffed endotracheal tube

question: An 11-year-old girl presented to the clinic with complaints of difficulty walking and bilateral symmetrical lower limb weakness. Past medical history revealed a recent gastrointestinal upset. On examination, power was reduced in both limbs and the deep tendon reflexes were absent. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed an increase in total protein concentration without pleocytosis. What is the most likely diagnosis?

An 8-year-old girl presents to the outpatient department with complaints of spontaneous bruising and petechiae all over the body. There is no history of hemarthrosis, mucosal bleeding, drug intake, or trauma. Past medical history reveals a recent episode of sore throat. Laboratory investigations show a prolonged bleeding time and a platelet count of 40,000/mm3. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 5-year-old child presents to the outpatient department with complaints of bilateral knee and shin pain for the past few weeks. The child also complains of fatigue, low-grade fever, and weight loss. On examination, the body temperature is 38.7°C (101.6°F) and there is generalized lymphadenopathy with mild hepatosplenomegaly. A complete blood count shows elevated white cell count, low platelets, and low hemoglobin. Based on these clinical findings what is your provisional diagnosis?
Which of the following is a poor prognostic factor in the case of acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL)?
Which of the following is the most common primary site for tuberculosis infection?

A 26-year-old woman has just delivered a healthy baby after an elective cesarean section indicated due to breach presentation. A few minutes after establishing a cry the baby becomes tachypneic with a respiratory rate of 65 breaths per minute, with chest recessions and nasal flaring. There is no gasping. What is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following is a side effect of ceftriaxone administration in children?

A 7-year-old child presents to the emergency department with blood in vomiting since morning. The child is a known case of Wilson's disease. It is suspected that the bleeding is secondary to oesophageal varices. What is the initial management in case of upper gastrointestinal bleeding?

answers.option: Immediate I/V fluid resuscitation, oxygen, monitoring of vitals

question: A 32-year-old woman known case of diabetes mellitus has just delivered a baby at the 37th week of gestation by a cesarean section. The baby cried immediately after birth but after an hour he develops sudden onset tachypnea with a rate of 66 breaths/min, nasal flaring, chest recessions, and expiratory grunt. What is the most likely diagnosis and what x-ray findings will accompany the respective diagnosis?

answers.option: Pneumothorax, air in the lower parts
Transient tachypnea of the newborn, streaky shadowing radiating out from the hila
Pneumothorax, air in the upper parts
Meconium aspiration syndrome, hilar shadows with streaky shadows and patchy atelectasis
Respiratory distress syndrome, ground glass appearance of the lung field with generalized atelectasis

question: A 2-year-old boy presents to the clinic with complaints of high-grade fever and cough for the past few days. The mother also informs the clinician that both his eyes have been red and tearing up occasionally. Now the child has developed a maculopapular rash that started from behind the ear and spread throughout his body. Upon further inquiry, it is found that the child is unvaccinated. What is the most likely cause of his rash?

A 13-month-old child presents to the emergency department with a complaint of diarrhea for one month. On examination, his eyes appear sunken, and the skin pinch goes back very slowly. How will you classify this patient on the basis of integrated management of neonatal and childhood illnesses (IMNCI)?

A 1-year-old child is brought to the emergency department with a complaint of loose stools for 3 days. On examination, the child is lethargic, has sunken eyes, his skin pinch goes back very slowly, and is not drinking water properly. How will you manage this child according to the Integrated Management of Newborn and Childhood Illness (IMNCI) guidelines?

answers.option: 100 mL/Kg IV of 5% dextrose over 6 hours
100 mL/Kg IV of Ringer's lactate over 6 hours

question: A 2-year-old child presents to the clinic with a complaint of difficulty feeding. On examination, his mid-upper-arm circumference is found to be less than 11 cm, and some palmar erythema is also observed. The child is able to finish ready-to-use therapeutic food (RUTF). How will you manage this child according to Integrated Management of Newborn and Childhood Illness (IMNCI) guidelines?

answers.option: Give IV glucose to treat low blood sugar

question: An electrocardiograph of a child shows rapid, irregular, bizarre QRS complexes of variable size and morphology. Which of the following is the drug of choice in the management of ventricular fibrillation?
An electrocardiograph of a child shows rapid, irregular, bizarre QRS complexes of variable size and morphology. What will be the immediate management?

answers.option: An IV bolus of 10 mg/Kg lignocaine

question: 2 days after being given the routine vaccination at the 10th week of life, the baby presents to the emergency department with complaints of fever and a generalized rash. On examination, the child is irritable, has a high-pitched cry, and has a fever of 101°F (38.3°C). Which component of the routine EPI vaccinations is responsible for the following presentation?

An 8-year-old child presents to the clinic with complaints of easy fatiguability, hunching posture, and poor vision, especially at night. On examination, the spine is kyphotic and there is severe corneal clouding. The physician also appreciates a murmur on the left side radiating to the axilla. Based on the clinical picture, which of the following is the appropriate diagnosis?
A mother brings her 7-month-old child to the clinic concerned about his growth and development. Which of the following activity corresponds best to his age?

answers.option: Head lag on pull to sit
Roll from prone to supine and pass things hand to hand

question: Which of the following vaccinations are administered to the child at 6 weeks of age according to the extended program of immunization (EPI)?

A 6-year-old boy presents to the clinic with complaints of recurrent chest infections. He has had 8 admissions due to this in the past 2 years. On further inquiry, the mother reveals that the child also has recurrent diarrhea with bulky, profuse, and foul-smelling stools on and off since birth. He is a product of consanguineous marriage. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 2-hour-old baby born prematurely at 31 weeks of gestation develops sudden onset tachypnea with a respiratory rate of 68 breaths/minute, expiratory grunting, and flaring of the alae nasi. The heart rate is 150 beats per minute and there is no cyanosis. What is the most likely diagnosis?
What is the management of pneumonia according to the integrated management of neonatal and childhood illness (IMNCI)?

A 6-year-old thin girl with a height of approximately 100 cm (3.2 ft) presents to the emergency department with severe dehydration, polydipsia, and, polyuria. On examination, the girl is irritable, non-cooperative, and feeds poorly. Laboratory findings include Na = 160 mEq/L, serum osmolality of 320 mOsm/Kg, low urine osmolality, and normal HbA1c levels. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 3-year-old is brought by his father with complaints of ear discharge and earache for the past 3 days. There is also a tender swelling behind the ear on the mastoid region. How will you classify this child on the basis of integrated management of neonatal and childhood illness (IMNCI) guidelines?

answers.option: Cannot classify on the basis of given information

question: An 11-year-old boy presents to the outpatient department with complaints of undocumented fever, body ache, and maculopapular rash on his face, trunk, and limbs that started from behind the ears and forehead. On examination, there are enlarged and tender posterior cervical and postauricular lymph nodes. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 6-year-old boy presents to the clinic with complaints of bilateral pedal edema and periorbital puffiness. He has just completed his course of steroid therapy for nephrotic syndrome 10 days ago. The patient also had a relapse 3 months back while tapering steroids. What is the correct terminology for this patient?

A 10-year-old female child presents to the clinic with complaints of recurrent mouth ulcers, an erythematous butterfly rash over the nose and cheeks, and alopecia. A systemic autoimmune disease is suspected. Which of the following is the best confirmatory test for the suspected disease?

answers.option: Increased C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate

question: An 8-year-old child comes to the clinic complaining of progressive muscle weakness and difficulty getting up from a sitting position. There is no associated pain, sensory deficits, or autonomic symptoms. The patient gives a history of steroid intake for some other disease for over a month. Which one of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A child presents to the outpatient department with complaints of joint pain in both knees, ankles, and wrists for 3 months. There is also swelling of these joints. It is suspected that the patient has juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA). Which of the following types of JIA should be suspected?

A 6-year-old child is brought to the emergency department due to excessive bleeding from a superficial, minor cut. Which of the following investigations will be ordered initially in order to reach a diagnosis?

answers.option: Complete blood count (CBC), bleeding time. prothrombin time (PT), activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT)
Levels of clotting factor VIII and XI

question: Parents bring their 8-month-old child to the clinic with the concern that their child does not look normal as compared to other kids his age. On examination, the child has coarse facial features with a wide nasal bridge, flattened midface, and a large forehead. There is also hepatosplenomegaly. Radiographic evidence shows the beaked appearance of the anteroinferior surface of the vertebrae, oar-shaped ribs, and irregular hyperostotic diaphysis and metaphysics. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 13-year-old boy presents to the clinic with complaints of recurrent chronic diarrhea and rectal bleeding for two years. Suspecting a lower gastrointestinal tract pathology a colonoscopy is ordered. The results show diffuse inflammation of the colon and superficial ulceration of the mucosa. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following statements corresponds best to typical febrile seizures?

answers.option: Seizures are associated with focal signs
Seizures last for more than 15 minutes

question: A 4-year-old boy presents to the emergency department with difficulty breathing preceded by an attack of rhinitis. On examination, there is prolonged expiration with expiratory wheezing and decreased breath sounds. Chest X-ray shows hyperinflation of lungs with patchy atelectasis. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 8-year-old female child is brought by her mother with the concern that her daughter is shorter than other kids her age. On examination, it is concluded that she has short stature and developmental delay. A complete blood count shows pancytopenia and macrocytic red blood cell. Which of the following statements is incorrect about the above-mentioned disease?

answers.option: It presents in the first decade of life
It is an autosomal recessive disorder
The disorder is not associated with any renal or cardiac abnormalities
Bone marrow trephine biopsy shows hypoplastic picture

question:
A 5-year-old child presented to the emergency department with complaints of epigastric pain and sudden loss of consciousness. He regained consciousness after a minute and then had abnormal, jerky, and unpurposeful body movements for a while. 
Which of the following was the most likely diagnosis?
A child presents to the outpatient department with complaints of short stature, bowing of the legs and alopecia . Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following is a cause of post-renal failure?
Which of the following is the drug of choice for infantile spasms?

A 5-year-old presents to the emergency department with complaints of severe abdominal pain. Laboratory investigations show blood glucose levels of  412 mg/dl.
Arterial blood gases are performed and the results show a pH of 7.0, pCO2 of 30 mmHg, and an HCO3 concentration of 15 mEq/L. Which of the following defects is the child suffering from?

An 8-year-old child presents to the emergency department with a complaint of hyperventilation. Arterial blood gases are advised and the results show a pH of 7.55, pCO2 of 25 mmHg, and an HCO3 concentration of 15 mEq/L. Which of the following defect is the child suffering from?

answers.option: Mixed respiratory acidosis and metabolic alkalosis

question: A 6-year-old girl comes to the clinic with scalp itching. On examination, greasy scales are noticed on the head and neck. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 2-year-old child presents to the clinic with a complaint of loose stools for 20 days. On examination, the child is lethargic and drinks water eagerly. His skin pinch goes back normally. How will you classify this patient according to the integrated management of neonatal and childhood illness (IMNCI)?

An infant born a few minutes ago now presents with difficulty breathing, irritability and sudden, involuntary jerks throughout the body. The child delivered via a spontaneous vaginal delivery after a prolonged difficult labour with trauma to the head. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 2-year-old presents to the emergency department with convulsions and edema of both feet and hands. On examination, his mid-upper arm circumference is 10.5 cm and the edema is pitting. His random blood sugar is 30 mg/dL. Keeping in mind that the child is a case of severe malnutrition what will be the next best step in the management of this child?

answers.option: Cover the child with a warm blanket and additional clothing
Broad spectrum antibiotics ampicillin and gentamycin
70 mL of ReSoMal per Kg bodyweight

question: A 7-year-old boy is brought to the emergency, the child is actively seizing. The parents inform you that this has been happening for at least 10 minutes. After assessment of the airway, breathing, and circulation an I/V line is set up and the blood is sent for all the relevant laboratory investigations. What is the next best step in the management of this patient?

answers.option: Wait for the seizure to resolve on its own, reassure parents

question: An 8-month-old baby born prematurely at the gestational age of 36 weeks now comes to the clinic for a routine check-up. The baby looks pale, is easily irritable, and weighs around 5.5 kilograms. A complete blood count is ordered which shows a total leucocyte count (TLC) 0f 8700/microlitres (lymphocytes = 45%, neutrophils = 50%, others = 2%), hemoglobin 4.3 g/L, mean corpuscular volume (MCV) 60 fL, mean corpuscular hemoglobin (MCH) 21 pg/cell, and mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration (MCHC) 24 % Hb/cell. Serum transferrin saturation is found to be less than 15%. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A child born into a vegan family received only a vegan diet after weaning with no intake of meat or eggs. The child now presents to the clinic with complaints of paraesthesia, convulsions, angular cheilosis, and glossitis. His complete blood count shows a picture of macrocytic anemia. Which of the following is the most likely cause?
A mother brings her 2-month-old child with concerns about ambiguous genitalia. On examination, the testis is impalpable. Which of the following investigations will help confirm the sex of the child?

A couple married for 1 year now comes to the clinic with a newly diagnosed pregnancy. They are concerned about the transmission of the beta thalassemia gene to their child since the two of them are first cousins. Which of the following tests do you recommend for the prenatal diagnosis of the disorder?

A 3-year-old child presents to the clinic with complaints of dysentery. On history, it is revealed that the child came in with the same complaint a few days back for which another healthcare worker gave him an antibiotic but the condition did not improve. 
How will you now manage the child according to the integrated management of newborn and childhood illness (IMNCI)?

answers.option: Change to second line oral antibiotic

question: A baby born a few hours ago now presents with respiratory distress, gasping, and cyanosis. On examination, the baby has a scaphoid-shaped slightly protuberant abdomen. His apex beat is shifted to the right side of the chest. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

answers.option: Congenital cystic disease of the lungs

question: A 3-year-old boy presents to the outpatient department with complaints of low-grade fever, noisy breathing on inspiration, and a barking cough with hoarseness. He had a respiratory infection a few days back. On examination, his temperature is 101°F (38.3°C) and his respiratory rate is 60 breaths/minute. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A baby born at 39 weeks of gestation goes into respiratory distress with an end-expiratory grunt, flaring of alae nasi, and cyanosis. There is also green-blackish discoloration on the skin, nails, and umbilicus. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A baby is delivered via a spontaneous vaginal delivery at 37 weeks of gestation. He does not establish respiration even after adequate warming and stimulation. The resuscitation team starts positive pressure ventilation (PPV) but the heart rate continues to fall until it is 60 beats per minute. The team then starts chest compressions but no improvement in heart rate is seen even after 60 seconds of continuous PPV with 100% oxygen and chest compressions. What should be the next step in the management of this child?

A baby born at 37 weeks of gestation fails to establish respiration and has a heart rate of 55 beats per minute even after adequate warming and stimulation. Positive pressure ventilation is started but the heart rate remains below 60 beats/minute after 30 seconds. What would be the next step in the management of this child?

A 5-year-old child is brought to the emergency department in an unconscious state. On examination, the child is not responding and his carotid pulse is not palpable. What is the next best step in the management of the child?

A 10-year-old boy presents to the clinic with a complaint of painful swelling in the retro-orbital area associated with fever. The pain increases on drinking lemon juice. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 10-year-old boy, who is a known case of diabetes mellitus type 1 comes to the clinic for his routine follow-up. He is currently taking subcutaneous insulin. The pediatrician reduces the dose of insulin and his condition improves. What is this phenomenon called?

A mother brings her 2-year-old child with complaints of short stature, failure to gain weight, and chronic diarrhea. The stools are bulky, foul-smelling, and pale. The complaints started around the time of weaning and the birth history is not significant. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following is the most common cause of intestinal obstruction in children?
An infant has presented with an umbilical hernia. Which of the following management options is most appropriate for this patient?

answers.option: Counsel about likely strangulation of the hernia
